newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai raw sugar premiums firm on lower crop figure.
newsitem.headline: Thai raw sugar premiums firm on lower crop figure.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums edged up slightly on government forecasts that the dry spell would sharply reduce sugar output for 1997/98, trade sources said on Monday.

Trade for distant contracts, especially for early 1998, was active with bids outnumbering offers as sellers were sidelined by uncertainties over production and anticipation that prices would rise further, they said.
"Millers were also reluctant to commit, afraid that they might not be able to meet the obligation," said a trader with a major Japanese trading house.
"Many also predicted that the crushing season could be delayed this year due to the impact of the erratic weather," he said. Thai mills normally start crushing cane in November.
Thailand's Cane and Sugar Board on Monday forecast that 1997/98 sugar cane output would fall to 48.4 million tonnes from 56.2 million in 1996/97.
Sugar output is expected to fall to 5.02 million tonnes on a tel quel basis versus 5.82 million in 1996/97.

With domestic demand estimated at 1.75 million tonnes, Thai sugar exports this year are likely to slide to 3.27 million tonnes from 1996/97's estimated 4.3 million, according to a senior board official.
The substantial drop was caused by a severe dry spell which hit various parts of Thailand during April-June.
"The sugar cane in central and eastern regions were hardest hit with 14.6 percent and 18.8 percent respectively of the crops being damaged," the official told Reuters.
Even though the board's figure already painted a bearish supply outlook, some in the industry said the forecast was too optimistic.
"I would say 45 million tonnes would be about it. Lots of ratoon were damaged during the dry spell and the improved rainfall now will have a limited impact," said a planters source.

Thai raw sugar premiums for July-September deliveries were quoted around 85/95 points (bid/offer) per pound over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange futures on an FOB basis, compared with 80/90 earlier this week.
January/March deliveries were quoted at 100/120 points per pound over New York, up slightly from last week. White sugar trade was quiet in a listless market, they said.
